page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-384-standardlssd-metal is a storage-optimized bare-metal server built on the x86_64 architecture. The platform delivers 384 dedicated vCPUs alongside 3072 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8 GB memory-to-core allocation. Because it operates as bare metal, workloads bypass virtualization overhead and gain direct execution access to hardware execution resources.

Storage configuration represents the central feature of this hardware type. The system incorporates 90,194 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage distributed across 12 local solid-state drives. It lacks discrete GPU accelerators, orienting its hardware design entirely toward data-intensive processing and local input/output density. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

In terms of qualitative cost efficiency and operational tradeoffs, the server provides extreme hardware density within a single node. Bundling over 90 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage and 3 TB of RAM avoids distributed storage network latency, making it cost effective for consolidated, IO-heavy installations. However, the absence of hardware accelerators and massive scale make it ill-suited for smaller, decoupled services.

Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-384-standardlssd-metal is designed for extreme scale enterprise databases, distributed analytics engines, real-time in-memory databases with heavy persistence needs, and large data warehousing workloads requiring massive local NVMe throughput.
description: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-384-standardlssd-metal is a high-density, storage-optimized bare-metal server engineered on the x86_64 architecture. The machine supplies 384 dedicated physical vCPUs paired with 3072 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per-core memory profile. Designed for substantial I/O requirements, it integrates 90,194 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity spread across 12 local drives, completely bypassing virtualization layers to maximize direct storage and CPU efficiency. The instance features zero discrete GPUs and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By consolidating 3 TB of memory with over 90 TB of attached low-latency NVMe solid-state storage, this bare-metal host serves high-throughput transactional databases, large-scale distributed analytics engines, extensive in-memory caching tiers requiring immediate local persistence, and mission-critical enterprise data warehouse infrastructure.
